# Fixed-normal mixed volume can have arbitrarily large positive Hessian index

This is an exact stopping test for a naive Alexandrov--Fenchel extension to mixed-integer volume. It retains a fixed full ambient set of facet normals, a fixed complete lattice base, positive fibers, and an open neighborhood of admissible support offsets. It makes no stationarity claim about depth. In particular it does not obstruct a theorem which additionally uses all actual critical cap equations.

## 1. One genuine common support deformation

Fix d>=2, N>=1, epsilon>0, and R=epsilon(N^2+1). Let K be any d-dimensional polytope containing zero in its interior, written irredundantly as

    K={x : u_i dot x<=1, i=1,...,f}.

At indices j=0,...,N define the affine roofs

    L_j(z)=R+epsilon j^2-2epsilon j z.

For h=(h_0,...,h_N) with |h_j|<epsilon/4, define the full ambient polytope

    C_h={ (z,x): 0<=z<=N,
             u_i dot x<=L_j(z)+h_j for every i,j }.       (1)

All ambient normals are fixed: the inequalities have normals (2epsilon j,u_i), in addition to the two base normals. The parameters vary only the support offsets, with the same h_j used across the continuous facets in roof group j.

Let ell_h(z)=min_j[L_j(z)+h_j]. It is concave and positive on [0,N], since

    L_j(z)=R-epsilon z^2+epsilon(z-j)^2
              >=R-epsilon N^2=epsilon.

Hence ell_h>=3epsilon/4, and the exact fiber of (1) at every real base is ell_h(z)K. The body is compact and full dimensional. Its complete integer base is exactly {0,...,N}.

At each integer k,

    L_j(k)-L_k(k)=epsilon(j-k)^2.

Even after the parameter perturbations, every j!=k has a positive gap at least epsilon/2. Thus the unique active roof at integer k is its own roof and

    (C_h)_k=(R-epsilon k^2+h_k)K.                       (2)

In particular each sampled fiber can vary its homothetic radius independently in this open parameter cube. Compatibility is guaranteed by the actual common inequality description, not by an unproved independent-fiber perturbation rule.

## 2. The exact mixed Hessian

Put V=|K|. The actual mixed volume is

    M(h)=V sum_(k=0)^N (R-epsilon k^2+h_k)^d.            (3)

Consequently

    partial_j partial_k M(h)=0          for j!=k,
    partial_k^2 M(h)=d(d-1)V
                        (R-epsilon k^2+h_k)^(d-2)>0.   (4)

Its Hessian is positive definite of rank N+1. This rank is arbitrarily large while the integer dimension remains n=1, whose parity count is only two. Thus neither a one-positive-direction Lorentzian signature nor a positive-index bound by 2^n holds for mixed volume under such fixed-normal support deformations.

The distinction from ordinary ambient volume is exact: ordinary volume integrates ell_h(z)^d over all real z, including the moving breakpoints of the roof. Mixed volume samples the unique active roof separately at each integer. Replacing this sum by the ordinary integral would erase the independent positive directions in (4).

## 3. What a cap-Hessian approach must additionally retain

For a fixed ambient cap H={a z+v dot x>=b}, let

    F(t)=|{x in K:v dot x>=t}|.

On any chamber where F is twice differentiable at the relevant thresholds, its sampled cap mass is

    mu_h(H)=sum_k r_k^d F((b-a k)/r_k),
    r_k=R-epsilon k^2+h_k.

Its Hessian is also diagonal in these support parameters. If xi_k=(b-a k)/r_k, the diagonal entry is

    r_k^(d-2)[d(d-1)F(xi_k)
              -2(d-1)xi_k F'(xi_k)+xi_k^2 F''(xi_k)].   (5)

This follows by differentiating the displayed one-variable summand twice. Purely full or empty fiber traces are included by their constant branches. At cap/facet transitions one must instead retain the correct one-sided chamber derivatives.

For example, if a=b=0 and K is a centered simplex with v a centroidal extremal direction, then mu_h(H)=Gamma_d M(h) identically. The raw mass and cap Hessians both have arbitrarily many positive directions, but their normalized difference is zero. The cap relation, rather than the signature of mass alone, is essential.

The admissible variation (1) therefore falsifies a blanket mixed-volume signature shortcut. It does not decide the reduced source-tie Hessian in `candidate 92662e9a8e20fd35`: that Hessian must still include actual critical caps, source relaxation, normalization, and the same menu-dependent source weights.

# Fixed-normal mixed volume can have arbitrarily large positive Hessian index

**Fixed ambient normals do not bound mixed-mass Hessian positive index**

Already with one integer coordinate and d>=2, compatible roof inequalities with a fixed common list of ambient facet normals realize independently variable sampled radii r_j. Their exact mixed mass is |K| sum_j r_j^d, whose Hessian is positive definite of arbitrarily large rank.

Scope limits: Refutes importing an ordinary Alexandrov-Fenchel signature bound for total mixed mass alone. It does not refute a cap-normalized Hessian theorem using all actual stationarity/source-tie constraints.
